name: GlassSurface-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The glass pane sits fully on the photo wall with its label readable and the bent image clearly visible inside.

tagline: A rounded glass pane drags across photos and bends them.
summary: A wall of eight photos fills the stage under huge white words. A frosted glass rectangle can be dragged around, magnifying and warping the pictures beneath it with faint colour fringes.
appearance: Eight photos sit in two rows on a dark stage with giant white words across the middle. A rounded rectangular glass pane, lightly frosted, holds two lines of white text and shows a bent, colour-edged copy of whatever sits behind it.
behaviour: Pressing and dragging the pane moves it over the photo wall, where the image inside shifts and magnifies with a slight rainbow edge. Releasing leaves it resting wherever it was dropped.
demo_content: Eight stock photos, the words 'Through the glass', and pane text 'Drag me around'.
search_phrases: frosted glass panel you can drag
apple liquid glass effect for web
rounded magnifier over a photo wall
see through pane with blurred edges
use_when: A card or panel should sit over imagery with a frosted, refracting finish instead of a flat fill.
avoid_when: Safari and Firefox skip the refraction filter, so those browsers get only a plain blur.
customise: Width, height, radius, border width, brightness, opacity, blur, displacement, background tint, saturation, distortion strength and blend mode are props.
weight_why: Per-channel SVG displacement plus backdrop filters on a small pane; still when not dragged.

a11y.note: The pane has focus styling but no tab stop, so it cannot be moved without a mouse, and it has no reduced-motion handling.

issues: The small pane text is hard to read whenever the glass passes over a bright photo.
Safari and Firefox skip the refraction filter, so the glass falls back to a plain blur there.
polish_why: A convincing liquid-glass pane over a rich photo wall; the tiny pane text fights bright photos.
title: GlassSurface
